universal_lens: Individual free throw success modeled as a multivariate stochastic process with trajectory parameters: launch angle, velocity, backspin, initial height, and lateral deviation. Logistic regression framework for free throw success modeling via standardized predictors and deviance-based variable selection.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference framework maps observed trajectory parameters to latent player skill and error distributions using conformal predictive intervals for real-time shot quality assessment. Bayesian inference on player-specific free throw probabilities using conformal predictive distributions derived from logistic models.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning engine uses state-transition models to predict optimal adjustments in release angle and velocity based on current player biomechanics and historical miss patterns. Situational reasoning engine maps real-time shot parameters to dynamic state transitions in free throw execution via multi-factor regression.

primitives.name: DirkNowitzkiFreeThrowAnalysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: This figure shows the probability distributions on a density scale of parameter estimates (backspin, launch height, launch velocity, launch angle, and left-right deviation) for Dirk Nowitzki's made and missed free throws, as well as all attempts combined.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Backspin: rotations per second (rot/s); Launch Height: meters (m); Launch Velocity: meters per second (m/s); Launch Angle: degrees ($^\circ$); Left-Right Deviation: meters (m)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes normally distributed shot trajectories, independent parameter measurements, and constant shooter skill over the sample period.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Applies to small sample sizes with binary outcomes (made/missed), transitioning to large-sample asymptotic normality via Central Limit Theorem.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's multivariate Bayesian hierarchical model for player-specific shot quality assessment, where posterior distributions of kinematic parameters inform probabilistic shot outcome predictions.
layer2.telemetry: Observed vs. expected free throw success rates conditional on kinematic deciles, serving as conformal prediction intervals.

primitives.name: SingleFactorImprovement
primitives.verbatim_quote: Note that each player usually has only one or two areas where their makes and misses differ, suggesting that it is indeed possible for them to improve by focusing on consistency in the relevant factor(s).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Consistency: standard deviation of parameter estimates (rot/s, m, m/s, $^\circ$, m)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes fixed underlying skill level, additive Gaussian noise in measurement, and independence between shot outcomes given parameters.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Applicable when variance components are separable, breaking down in highly correlated error structures.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's state-transition framework for situational reasoning, where a single actionable kinematic variable (e.g., release angle) serves as a control input to shift the system from 'miss' to 'make' basin of attraction.
layer2.telemetry: Pre-post standard deviation reduction in target parameter, validated against longitudinal change in free throw percentage.

primitives.name: DirectionalBiasCorrection
primitives.verbatim_quote: Like Nowitzki, Brendan Haywood, Luis Scola, Shawn Marion, and Richard Jefferson also have a problem with left-right deviation, though Jefferson's missed shots tend to drift left, whereas the others all drift right.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Left-Right Deviation Bias: meters (m), signed quantity indicating direction
primitives.assumptions: Assumes systematic directional bias exists within individual shooter's error distribution, not purely random scatter.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if biases reverse sign over time due to coaching interventions or physical changes.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's conformal prediction framework for directional bets, where a player's consistent leftward drift becomes a predictable feature for wagering on shot chart positions.
layer2.telemetry: Signed distance from centerline of rim for each miss, aggregated into mean bias estimate with confidence bounds.

primitives.name: ShotFlatnessProblem
primitives.verbatim_quote: (Each of the twenty players under consideration are right-handed shooters except for Manu Ginobili.) Tony Parker, Chuck Hayes, and Ginobili's misses are all too flat and have too much backspin.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Shot Flatness: complementary angle to launch angle relative to optimal arc (e.g., 90° - optimal angle)
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a trade-off between launch angle and backspin, holding energy and spin axis constant.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when shooter compensates for flatness by adjusting grip or stroke mechanics, decoupling the relationship.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's multi-stage decision process, where a flat shot triggers a cascade of corrective actions (e.g., adjusting elbow angle) to restore proper trajectory.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal sequence analysis of consecutive shots, identifying transition probabilities from 'flat' state to 'corrected' state.

primitives.name: Left-Right Miss Classification

primitives.assumptions: Misses are categorized spatially into left/right bins with distinct underlying causes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Spatial misalignment in release trajectory leads to directional deviation.

layer2.mapping: Each miss type corresponds to a distinct latent variable in the logistic model.
layer2.telemetry: Directional deviation metrics from shot tracking data.

primitives.name: Deviance-Based Variable Selection
